# Independent audit: functional normal-cone injection and cap profiles

Audited source: `candidate c2528b1460a23da4`, Sections 1--6. Result: PASS, conditional only on the explicitly cited, already proved finite-support normal-cone injection.

The finite partitions in that injection are Borel (continuous linear comparisons with a fixed tie rule); their translated pieces remain Borel and are pairwise disjoint. Translation invariance of H_q therefore transfers the weighted integral exactly, not just the unweighted measure. The assumption that g is Borel avoids the nonmeasurable-infimum issue. Nonnegative bounded functions suffice, and nonnegative extended functions follow by the same integral comparison. The compact sums A+B and compact cylinder base plus a linear subspace are Borel; in finite dimensions the latter cylinder is closed. The epsilon=1/j source sets increase to A minus V, so source-only monotone convergence applies without requiring any convergence of selected translations.

The affine-subspace reduction in Section 2 translates A, P, the affine subspace and the argument of F by the same vector, while leaving B unchanged. Thus the original integral statement is restored exactly. The baseline P+B lies entirely in the cylinder, disjoint from every injected target piece. No repeated-baseline addition is asserted.

For Section 3, v_i.a<-1 and v_i.b<=1 imply v_i.(a+b)<0, so the Boolean incidence implication is coordinatewise and is preserved by every increasing Psi. Zero-level signs are unchanged under positive dilation by 1/2, giving the exact factor 2^d. The affine hull of P has zero ambient d-volume, so omitting it from the source integral loses no mass. The mixed intrinsic variant correctly retains that mass and needs a common integer parity class for its chosen midpoints; it claims only 2^q, not a Gamma improvement.

The OR, AND and clipped-count choices are all increasing Boolean functions. In Section 5 the residual regions R_j are pairwise disjoint: membership in two of them would force every circuit inequality strictly negative, contradicting sum v_i=0. Every selected P_j+B lies in the corresponding zero-level residual region, and each has volume |B|. Thus the baseline lower bound kb and the full actual baseline integral are valid. The note correctly identifies the simple marginal sum consequence as weaker than separate Brunn--Minkowski.

Finally, in the planar circuit, away from the three null boundary lines N_K is exactly one or two. Hence integral (N_K-1)_+=integral N_K-k=2k-3Q+sum U_i. On A, three simultaneously missed strict thresholds are impossible; excess count above one is exactly the indicator of the disjoint unique-capture residual regions. Substitution into the SAME-baseline functional inequality proves (8), with all factors and signs correct. No scalar realization or missing lower bound for the actual baseline profile is silently supplied.
